evidenceLaw.maintainerPosts: Authoritative for maintainer intent, boundaries, plans, explanations, and status claims only.
evidenceLaw.communityPosts: Requirements, proposals, observations, and bug reports only; never source or runtime proof.

claims.statement: A production editor for Japanese and other CJK content needs vertical writing, including editor-owned caret behavior where contenteditable is unreliable.
claims.author: karintou8710
claims.topicTitle: Any plans for vertical writing mode support?

claims.statement: Vertical writing had not received serious design work because the maintainer did not know there was concrete demand.
claims.author: marijn
claims.topicTitle: Any plans for vertical writing mode support?

claims.statement: Modern Japanese vertical writing requires mixed-orientation text, ruby, tate-chu-yoko, reliable IME, and browser-independent caret behavior.
claims.author: karintou8710
claims.topicTitle: Any plans for vertical writing mode support?

claims.statement: Vertical writing is outside the maintained core; a custom editor component or fork may reuse Wordgard data structures.
claims.author: marijn
claims.topicTitle: Any plans for vertical writing mode support?

claims.statement: Offline collaborative editing needs durable reconciliation beyond Wordgard's real-time central-authority transform loop.
claims.author: thesmartwon

claims.statement: Offline automatic merging is primarily a change-review and adjustment UI problem, not just a merge-algorithm problem.
claims.author: marijn

claims.statement: Fractional indices do not provide stable document addressing by themselves; durable addressing requires element IDs and tombstones, which often cost more than they return.
claims.author: marijn

claims.statement: Candidate offline designs include a causal transaction oplog with snapshots or SQL tables using ordered IDs and fractional insertion positions.
claims.author: thesmartwon

claims.statement: Building the footnote example exposed and triggered fixes for block nodes that behave as atoms.
claims.author: marijn

claims.statement: A collaborative-editing example and accompanying explanation were published.
claims.author: marijn

claims.statement: Switching between footnotes in Firefox could display stale nested content unless selection state changed.
claims.author: mhmttosun

claims.statement: The maintainer reported pushing a patch for the stale-footnote-content report.
claims.author: marijn

claims.statement: The first footnote patch introduced a runtime crash because contentEq was unavailable.
claims.author: mhmttosun

claims.statement: The crash came from example code using an unpublished method absent from the website's installed library version.
claims.author: marijn

claims.statement: A user reported that the corrected footnote example worked.
claims.author: mhmttosun

claims.statement: Porting realistic ProseMirror examples is intentionally used to discover missing Wordgard behavior, with more examples planned.
claims.author: marijn

claims.statement: An external SQL model may need bidirectional conversion between editor transactions and database transactions.
claims.author: thesmartwon

claims.statement: Stable per-word identity and large-document performance create tension between node-per-word DOM rendering and compact text projection.
claims.author: thesmartwon

claims.statement: An update listener can observe editor activity for outbound synchronization, while external changes can be pushed into the editor.
claims.author: marijn

claims.statement: Mapped range metadata can keep information about document spans outside the document, while schema nodes may be simpler when identity is structural.
claims.author: marijn

claims.statement: Database transaction mapping and virtualization remain linked requirements for large documents with stable external identities.
claims.author: thesmartwon

claims.statement: Wordgard exists to revisit and improve unresolved design problems in ProseMirror rather than preserve that architecture unchanged.
claims.author: marijn

claims.statement: Wordgard deliberately prefers functional algebraic state design and facets over Lexical-style imperative composition.
claims.author: marijn
claims.topicTitle: How does this compare to the Lexical editor by Meta?

claims.statement: Large documents and expensive node views motivate bounded DOM mounting, but nested variable-height content makes naïve list windowing insufficient.
claims.author: strogonoff

claims.statement: Core virtualization is intentionally excluded because its code and API complexity impose a tax on most users.
claims.author: marijn

claims.statement: Wordgard data structures are intended for reuse by canvas, native, React, or virtualizing editor components, but the host abstractions still need real adopters and refinement.
claims.author: marijn

claims.statement: Native ESM namespaces could avoid TypeScript namespace declaration problems and improve tree shaking, but lose callable-class-plus-namespace ergonomics.
claims.author: ocavue
claims.topicTitle: API design: TS Namespace vs ESM `export * as ns`

claims.statement: TypeScript namespaces were selected to support nested classes; an ESM alternative was considered.
claims.author: marijn
claims.topicTitle: API design: TS Namespace vs ESM `export * as ns`

claims.statement: Splitting every nested API into ESM modules creates awkward ownership and cycles, so Wordgard keeps namespaces and rewrites build output for tree shaking.
claims.author: marijn
claims.topicTitle: API design: TS Namespace vs ESM `export * as ns`

claims.statement: A Vite consumer observed the link namespace missing at runtime.
claims.author: keais
claims.topicTitle: API design: TS Namespace vs ESM `export * as ns`

claims.statement: The missing link API was attributed to a namespace-mangling build bug that let dead-code elimination drop a live namespace.
claims.author: marijn
claims.topicTitle: API design: TS Namespace vs ESM `export * as ns`

claims.statement: A non-browser Rust port needs the document and command substrate to be separable from DOM layout and selection.
claims.author: nicoburns

claims.statement: Host independence was a deliberate design goal, but it remains unproven until another host drives a generic subset of the editor interface.
claims.author: marijn

claims.statement: Users want a Wordgard Markdown parser and serializer equivalent to the ProseMirror module.
claims.author: kepta

claims.statement: Markdown serialization is not a core priority and is expected to live in a separate module.
claims.author: marijn

claims.statement: Framework users need to render Angular-owned components inside editor content.
claims.author: mariojsnunes
claims.topicTitle: Any plan to render Angular components inside the editor?

claims.statement: Core widgets may host custom DOM, while Angular and other framework adapters stay outside the core library.
claims.author: marijn

proposedMatrixRows.mechanism: Project vertical-rl/vertical-lr lines, ruby, tate-chu-yoko, and mixed-orientation runs into visual geometry and navigation.
proposedMatrixRows.title: CSS vertical-rl/lr layout, ruby, mixed orientation, geometry, and navigation
proposedMatrixRows.whyNew: CSS vertical layout, ruby, tate-chu-yoko, and horizontal runs inside vertical lines are not the same concept as bidi text direction or ordinary geometry mapping.

proposedMatrixRows.mechanism: Route vertical-writing caret motion, selection, keyboard intent, composition, and IME reconciliation independently from horizontal bidi input.
proposedMatrixRows.title: Vertical-mode caret, selection, key routing, composition, and IME reconciliation
proposedMatrixRows.whyNew: Caret motion and composition in vertical writing have independent browser failure modes and proof obligations from layout projection.

proposedMatrixRows.mechanism: Expose offline divergence as attributed changes that a user can review, accept, reject, and adjust after convergence.
proposedMatrixRows.title: User-visible offline change attribution, review, and adjustment atop convergence
proposedMatrixRows.whyNew: Offline reconciliation is a user-visible review workflow, not merely the existing real-time OT or Yjs transport loop.

proposedMatrixRows.mechanism: Define a typed headless editor capability that DOM, React, virtualized, native, and canvas hosts can consume without depending on a specific view class.
proposedMatrixRows.title: Typed headless editor capability across DOM, React, virtualized, native, and canvas hosts
proposedMatrixRows.whyNew: A command-capable editor interface shared by DOM, native, canvas, React, and virtualized views is more specific than package entrypoints or one imperative DOM view lifecycle.

proposedMatrixRows.mechanism: Own Markdown parsing and serialization in a separate package that integrates with the editor through host codecs.
proposedMatrixRows.title: Separately owned Markdown parse/serialize module integrated through host codecs
proposedMatrixRows.whyNew: Markdown parsing and serialization ownership is absent from the current matrix and is independent from the DOM/HTML codec.

proposedMatrixRows.mechanism: Observe committed editor transactions and snapshots for outbound synchronization and apply inbound external-model transactions through the editor update boundary.
proposedMatrixRows.title: Bidirectional external-model synchronization over committed editor transactions
proposedMatrixRows.whyNew: Observing editor transactions and applying external database changes is a distinct integration contract from state fields, commit impact queries, or collaboration transport.
